log.msg: vision-report's operative finding for this task: per-image vision cost is dominated by context accumulation, not the image (~1.3-4k tokens each). A resumed session re-reads every prior image as cache-read, so cost grows with the SQUARE of image count. One fresh session per image keeps it flat. Confirms Mike's hypothesis — capture in one session, analyze in N fresh ones.

Calibration targets from cross-model consensus: rails clipped at 400px with no scroll affordance; prose measure ~95-130ch at 1920 against a documented 52em spec; 39-45% dead right-hand space at 3440. All three are expressible as dimensionless ratios — which is the thesis of the JS-first analyzer.

log.msg: SECURITY (pre-existing, now fixed): the dev SocketServer created its WebSocketServer with no verifyClient and no Origin check. A WebSocket upgrade is not subject to the same-origin policy, so ANY page in any tab could open ws://localhost and speak the protocol — which includes rpc:cmd (child_process.exec), rpc:write, and now rpc:ask (a Claude turn with unrestricted tools). That is arbitrary command execution on this machine from any site visited while the dev server runs. Added a local_only verifyClient to Server/plugins/SocketServer/SocketServer.js: a browser always sends Origin, a CLI tool sends none, and a local process already has everything the check would protect. Verified: foreign origin 401, localhost accepted, no-origin accepted, live-reload still connects.

log.msg: CALIBRATED: 64/64 on the corpus at 400/1280/1920/3440. Every bad case trips its named rule at every width it applies to; no good case produces a high-severity finding at any width. Getting there took six false-positive classes out of the rules — inline boxes and display:contents (clientWidth 0), scrollers, deliberate crops, full-bleed shells, and code. All recorded in knowledge/false-positives.md.

The tool found a bug in our own documented advice. The Good widescreen case was written straight from the layout-design skill (.grid.auto with --column: 40em) and FAILED at 1280 with 112 characters a line: auto-fill with a 1fr maximum is unbounded, so at one column the track takes the whole width. 1fr is right for tiles, wrong for prose — a reading column needs minmax(min(34em,100%), 38em), bounded at both ends. Skill needs updating.

assign.now: Site audit re-running with corrected hit-size; writing the findings report

log.msg: First full-site audit (116 pages x 1280/3440) exposed two analyzer faults before it exposed anything about the site. hit-size fired 4274 times across every page: inline links in prose are sized by the line (WCAG 2.5.8 exempts them), and a.page-preview-link is 105x13 with an ::after stretched over the whole card — its rect understates the target tenfold. The probe now asks getComputedStyle(el, "::after") whether a pseudo enlarges the hit area. Second: 78 of 116 pages scored exactly 0, so the score could not rank anything — one rule can now cost at most 25 points, because a site-wide habit should cost a grade, not the whole scale.

Vision integration works and CONFIRMS the numbers rather than replacing them. ext/LayoutTool/vision.js hands Claude the screenshot AND the numeric findings and asks which it can actually see. On /framework/ext/LayoutTool/ it independently confirmed the measure findings — "the prose paragraph and the bullet list items both visibly run the full content width, matching what the analyzer flagged" — in 14.8s for $0.097. Read-only by construction (tools: Read,Glob,Grep); a prompt typed into a page must not be able to write to this repo.

Vision also caught a bug the numbers could not: the tool page measured itself on the next animation frame, before any md() had resolved, so it reported 50 nodes and a row of em-dashes. The screenshot showed a half-empty page and Claude said so. Now settles 450ms, the same way frame() does.

sweep() verified: 13 samples + bisect over 400-3440 in ~10s, and it earns its keep immediately — on the Good widescreen case it found an illegible band that exists ONLY between ~840 and ~1208px. That is exactly the in-between width Mike asked about, and no amount of checking 400/1280/1920/3440 would have found it. First version reported four edges where there was one, because the signature included width_used in 5% buckets: a continuous metric does not become discrete by bucketing it, it just crosses a boundary every few hundred px.

The largest single source of noise, and the one guard that is a POLICY rather than a measurement: ext/demo's stage simulates a different viewport at a different zoom, so measuring its contents as part of the host page compares two viewports. Left in, the layouts pages reported 460-502 high findings each and illegible fired 7173 times — all 3px text inside 0.25x miniatures that have a zoom control directly above them. There is no intrinsic difference between a deliberate miniature and text someone shrank by mistake, so the tool is TOLD, by selector: probe.IGNORE covers .demo-screen, .demo-sims, .page-preview-thumb and [data-layout-ignore]. Reversible with { ignore: "[data-layout-ignore]" }.

assign.now: Final audit run; then the model-vs-numbers comparison

log.msg: SITE AUDIT, 116 framework pages at 1280 and 3440. Grades at 1280: 8 A, 32 B, 21 C, 22 D, 33 F. The dominant real finding is ONE HABIT: over-wide prose on 76 pages — 257 high-severity and 317 medium measure findings, lines running 95-150 characters against the 52em/~75ch the site documents. That independently reproduces what Sonnet and Opus both reported about these pages yesterday from screenshots. Behind it: escape (27 high / 27 pages), zero-size (27/27), doc-overflow (23/23), cramped low (634 across 40 pages), hit-size (216 medium across all 116 — mostly button.mode-btn at 21px and the layout range sliders at 17px).

FINAL AUDIT — 232 runs, 0 errors. 1280px: 8 A, 32 B, 21 C, 22 D, 33 F. 3440px: 16 A, 12 B, 33 C, 26 D, 29 F. Worst at 1280 are the Page/overview/* docs pages (F 29-42, 4-6 high measure each) and ext/Panel (F 41, 12 high). Rules that fire site-wide: measure (255 high / 324 med / 76 pages), escape (27/27), zero-size (27/27), doc-overflow (23/23), cramped low (639/40), hit-size med (216, all 116 pages). At 3440 dead-space appears on 55 pages and measure worsens to 330 high — the site gets WIDER prose on a wider screen rather than more columns.

MODEL COMPARISON, 8 corpus cases, fresh session per image, no ground truth in the prompt. Opus 8/8 ($0.95, 49s). Sonnet 7/8 ($1.45, 41s). Haiku 6/8 ($0.27, 57s). LayoutTool 8/8, free, 0.3s. The case that separates them is the one the tool was built for: cramped-card (three bordered cards with padding 0). Haiku AND Sonnet both answered fine; Opus caught it — "the cards have no padding, so their heading and body text sit flush against the card borders". The analyzer measures a 0.00x frame gap. General shape: overlap, clipping and grossly long lines are visually loud and every model got them; a missing 12px of padding is visually quiet and two of three missed it, while being numerically the least ambiguous finding in the set. No model produced a false alarm on the clean pages.

assign.outcome: **ext/LayoutTool landed** — a numeric layout analyzer (13 rules, every threshold a dimensionless ratio) scoring 64/64 against a 16-case ground-truth corpus at 400/1280/1920/3440px, with no AI at runtime. Site audit: 232 runs, 0 errors; the dominant real finding is one habit — over-wide prose on 76 of 116 pages (255 high-severity measure findings at 1280, 330 at 3440), independently confirmed by three vision models. Also shipped: a width sweep that bisects for edge-case widths (found an illegible band existing only between 840-1208px), a knowledge base of five lessons indexed by the readme, a before/after audit page whose Accept writes to a review queue rather than site CSS, and a read-only Claude second-opinion button. Updated the /layout-design skill — including correcting its own advice, which the tool disproved. **Also fixed a pre-existing security hole**: the dev WebSocket server had no Origin check, so any site visited while the dev server ran could reach rpc:cmd (exec) — arbitrary command execution on this machine.

log.msg: Two bugs found by looking at the tool's OWN before/after panes. (1) .lt-twin used .grid.auto, which is auto-fit + 1fr, and generated a THIRD empty track at 1700px — leaving the pair huddled in the left two-thirds. A pair is a pair at every width; it now declares two tracks and stacks below 56em. Same family as the 1fr bug the corpus found in the skill. (2) measure still fired inside code: excluding by tag name let every highlighted span.hljs-* through, so a syntax-coloured string reported as a 129-character line and the proposed fix was max-width on a token. Now excluded by ANCESTRY, not tag.

Baseline regenerated after the two self-audit fixes — 232 runs, 0 errors, findings.json 497KB. Corrected numbers supersede the landing line: measure is 238 high / 316 medium across 64 pages at 1280 (was 255/76 — the drop is the highlighted-code false positives leaving). Grades at 1280: 9 A, 32 B, 20 C, 22 D, 33 F. Proposals now read sensibly: `p { max-width: 52em }` is the fix for the dominant finding, where before the fix it was offering `span.hljs-string { max-width: 52em }`.
